name: Kubernetes container runs privileged
description: A container is configured with securityContext.privileged: true, which disables container isolation and gives the process effectively full access to the host.
recommendation: Remove privileged: true and grant only the specific Linux capabilities the workload needs.
must-match:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      securityContext:
        privileged: true
must-not-match:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      securityContext:
        privileged: false

name: Kubernetes container allows privilege escalation
description: allowPrivilegeEscalation is true, so a process in the container can gain more privileges than its parent, for example through a setuid binary. The Restricted Pod Security Standard requires this to be false.
recommendation: Set allowPrivilegeEscalation: false in the container securityContext.
must-match:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      securityContext:
        allowPrivilegeEscalation: true
must-not-match:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      securityContext:
        allowPrivilegeEscalation: false

name: Kubernetes pod shares a host namespace
description: hostPID, hostIPC or hostNetwork is enabled. Sharing a host namespace lets the container inspect host processes through /proc, attach to host shared memory, or observe host network traffic. All three are disallowed by the Baseline and Restricted Pod Security Standards.
recommendation: Remove the setting. If a node-level agent genuinely requires it, isolate that workload to a dedicated node pool.
must-match:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  hostPID: true
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  hostNetwork: true
must-not-match:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  hostPID: false

name: Kubernetes container root filesystem is writable
description: readOnlyRootFilesystem is explicitly false, so an attacker who achieves execution can modify the container image at runtime, for example by replacing a binary on the PATH.
recommendation: Set readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and mount an emptyDir or a volume for the paths that must be writable.
must-match:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      securityContext:
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
must-not-match:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      securityContext:
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: true

name: Kubernetes container may run as root
description: runAsNonRoot is explicitly false, which permits the container to run as uid 0. The requirement states containers must run as a non-root user, and gives 10001 as the default uid and gid.
recommendation: Set runAsNonRoot: true and give runAsUser a high, non-zero uid such as 10001.
must-match:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: false
must-not-match:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true

name: Kubernetes container image is unpinned
description: The image tag is latest, or no tag is given, so the image that runs is whatever the registry resolves at pull time. That defeats the verified-image requirement and makes a deployment unreproducible.
recommendation: Pin the image by digest, for example image: contoso/app@sha256:..., or at minimum to an immutable version tag.
must-match:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: contoso/app:latest
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: contoso/app
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: localhost:5000/team/app
must-not-match:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: contoso/app@sha256:0123456789abcdef
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: contoso/app:1.2.3
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: localhost:5000/team/app:1.2.3

name: Kubernetes container adds a dangerous capability
description: SYS_ADMIN grants a large fraction of root's powers, and SYS_PTRACE allows attaching to and reading the memory of other processes. The requirement calls for both to be dropped.
recommendation: Drop ALL capabilities and add back only the minimum the workload needs.
must-match:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      securityContext:
        capabilities:
          add:
            - SYS_ADMIN
must-not-match:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      securityContext:
        capabilities:
          drop:
            - ALL

name: Kubernetes pod mounts a host path
description: A hostPath volume mounts a file or directory from the node into the pod, which bypasses container isolation. Writing to it can affect other pods or persist on the node.
recommendation: Use a ConfigMap, Secret, emptyDir or PersistentVolumeClaim. Where a host path is unavoidable, restrict it with an allowed-paths policy.
must-match:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  volumes:
    - name: hostvol
      hostPath:
        path: /var/log
must-not-match:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  volumes:
    - name: cfg
      configMap:
        name: app-config
